policy: Preserve business ownership and public behavior while replacing platform mechanisms. These mappings identify implemented native coverage and explicit remaining gaps; they are not a file-count completion percentage. No source file is declared fully equivalent.

groups.name: Renderer Agent controllers
groups.remaining: The Renderer application layer is ported over a generic AgentClientPort (product method names) and a UiRuntime (window executor; a paused tokio clock in tests): AgentSessionController with its typed StatePatch and derived control state, the display replica (attach/ACK coalescing/watermark/bounded recovery with silent→reconnecting→degraded stages), session preparation, lifecycle, turn submission intents and reference drafts. Async methods do their synchronous prefix eagerly and keep running un-awaited, like JS promises. The product session-feed suite passes against the real Main service harness, and 44 of the 45 controller tests pass over the ported withDisplayFeed fixture (Main control/transcript reducers); the remaining one drives the item-host process service. AgentControllerRegistry and ConversationHistoryController pass their product suites, as does the session UI store. The submission-lifecycle, reference-draft, prompt-mention and workspace-path suites pass too. Remaining: the window client over AgentHostHandle, and moving the GPUI views off the legacy controller.

groups.name: Native platform client
groups.remaining: In-process native composition now routes Codex, Claude, ACP providers, Pi and the Rust PuppyOne runtime. Complete Electron setup/account/installation services are not represented by this port.

groups.name: Chat presentation
groups.remaining: Native virtual transcript, CommonMark, tables/code/copy, attachment/image previews, commands, typed approval/question/MCP forms, history filtering and controls exist. Mermaid graphics, all provider activity renderers, inline file navigation, accessibility and pixel parity remain pending.

groups.name: Agent workbench items
groups.remaining: Project-retained entities and persisted validated tabs/splits/native identities exist; restart uses explicit resume and never replays terminal commands. Formal RootId/session-registry integration, exact preparation leases and visual drag/drop parity remain pending.

groups.name: Codex runtime and protocol
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the AgentRuntimeAdapter port with the product adapter and paginated-history tests (FakeConnection via connectionFactory). Discovery (codex-discovery, executable discovery) and the runtime definition are pending; the running app still uses legacy_codex_app_server_adapter.rs until the Agent host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: Bounded native JSONL transport
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 with an injectable spawner and the product transport tests. The Codex/ACP/Pi adapters still use legacy_jsonl_rpc_connection.rs until they move onto the new runtime port.

groups.name: Native installation inventory
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 with the product inventory tests (deduplicated scans, five-minute cache, sanitized 24-hour persisted snapshot, Refresh superseding an in-flight scan, per-tool failure isolation) and the connection-policy characterization regenerated from the product (26 cases). The executable-candidate and process-budget cases run with platform/local_agent_installation. The app's Settings and setup still read legacy_local_agent_inventory.rs until the host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: ACP protocol core
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the AgentRuntimeAdapter port (bootstrap, history replay, permission/question correlation, workspace file delegate, config options) with the product ACP client, history-replay and prompt-input tests. The fileSystemFactory injection is replaced by the real Main file delegate. The app still runs legacy_acp_runtime_adapter.rs until the host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: Pi RPC protocol core
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the AgentRuntimeAdapter port with the product Pi RPC client, event-normalizer and prompt-input tests (scripted process). The app still runs legacy_pi_rpc_adapter.rs until the host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: Claude Agent SDK runtime
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the AgentRuntimeAdapter port with the product adapter, events, spawn and prompt-input tests. claude_agent_sdk/ is the Rust equivalent of @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.159 (stream-json control protocol, listSessions/getSessionInfo/getSessionMessages/forkSession); its session helpers match the official SDK on real transcripts, and the initialization handshake is verified against Claude Code 2.1.291. The app still runs legacy_claude_adapter.rs until the host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: Product-owned PuppyOne runtime
groups.remaining: The Main-side modules are ported 1:1 over the shared Pi RPC adapter (model-connection lease binding, private fd-3 configuration bootstrap, read-only history resume, image capability gate, worker discovery and probe contract, narrow worker environment, versioned approval envelope) with the Main-side kernel tests. The JS worker on the pinned Pi SDK (worker/*.mjs) is neither bundled nor reimplemented: by decision (2026-11-06) the Built-in Agent keeps running on the legacy native Rust harness (adapter.rs, model_client.rs, session_store.rs, tools.rs) until the kernel question is revisited.

groups.name: Reference ingestion
groups.remaining: agent-reference-authorization and the attachment store are ported 1:1 with the product authorization and attachment-store tests: live workspace references re-canonicalized per turn with a shared 32-file/25 MB budget and portable root-independent ids; external files and pathless inline bytes copied into private 0600 snapshots bound to owner, workspace and draft epoch, deduplicated, leased by one turn, expired, revoked and swept with the staging of exited processes, with TOCTOU detection and transactional batch rollback. agent-attachment-store.mjs is a deprecated re-export. The composer still uses legacy_attachments.rs until the host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: Session catalog and capacity
groups.remaining: The conversation catalog and session repository are ported 1:1 with the product catalog, catalog-concurrency and repository tests (serialized read/modify/persist, atomic owner-only replacement, memory published only after the rename, malformed files preserved, native identity partitioned by source scope, ICU-ordered records). The session lease still limits sessions to eight per workspace and 32 per application; the app keeps legacy_session_catalog.rs until the host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: Native rich transcript and composer
groups.remaining: Bounded virtual rows, native Markdown/table/code rendering, copy, previews, slash suggestions and per-thread drafts are implemented. Full renderer registry, Mermaid, inline assets, advanced autocomplete, accessibility and OS visual verification remain pending.

groups.name: Provider activities
groups.remaining: Provider notices are a bounded snapshot list (32, updated by id, labels 4000 characters, secrets redacted): Pi extension notify (severity as status, the extension as source) and Claude auth_status (system, authentication). The dock shows running/failed/warning lines and the rest under a closed Notifications N disclosure with source tooltips (chat-activities 98.9%). Compaction stays a status notice until the transcript renders system activities (G-3); the legacy :extension: activity normalisation has no native journal to read.

groups.name: Tool activity step lines
groups.remaining: Tool groups are step lines with their glyph, verb and subject, and three or more file reads fold into an Explored line, as the product; the evidence trees (AgentToolEvidenceTree, AgentToolTextEvidence) and the native model's missing durations remain.

groups.name: Shared Agent contract
groups.remaining: Every module is ported file by file over JSON values with JavaScript string/number/date semantics (src/agent/contract/js.rs). In-process requests carry Uint8Array bytes tagged as base64; dates without an offset parse as UTC instead of local time; display entries are shared Arc values with a weak per-entry size cache in place of the product's WeakMap. The TypeScript-only type files have no runtime counterpart beyond the accessors in types.rs.

groups.name: Main transcript projection
groups.remaining: Ported with the product's projection tests (desktop-agent.projection.test.ts). Test timelines read Main rows directly until the Renderer's transcript-rows builder is ported; object key order inside display entries can differ where the product spreads undefined values.

groups.name: Main session control and actor
groups.remaining: Control reducer, recovery, checkpointing, workspace paths and the SessionActor (single-threaded Rc handle with ordered re-entrant publication) are ported with the actor-level product tests. Windows path containment is not exercised on macOS; the service-level control tests arrive with the application layer.

groups.name: Event envelope and edit evidence
groups.remaining: Envelope creation, redaction and renderer bounds are ported; jsdiff structuredPatch is replaced by the similar crate (Myers line diff), whose hunk boundaries can differ from jsdiff on ambiguous edits. Cyclic payloads cannot occur in JSON values.

groups.name: Main Agent application service
groups.remaining: Every application module (service, session runtime/lifecycle/commands/feed, turns and queue, history indexer and queries, runtime resolution, process supervisor) is ported onto a single-threaded tokio LocalSet with the product's service and control tests. Project-session operation fences (operation.assertCurrent) are not wired yet; the IPC handlers, item-host process split and Renderer feed client arrive with the host layer.

groups.name: Main runtime port and registry
groups.remaining: The adapter port is a trait whose optional methods are named by implements(); requests and results stay plain objects. Concrete runtimes still run on the legacy adapter until each is ported onto this port.

groups.name: Session record and legacy format
groups.remaining: The session record keeps the product's derived getters over the SessionActor; the legacy snapshot model it replaces remains as domain/legacy_session_model.rs until the old UI and runtimes are removed.

groups.name: Codex reference input
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 (workspace text appendix, native localImage inputs, authorization errors) with the product cases; live wiring follows the runtime switch.

groups.name: Main security boundaries
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 over Node path semantics (node_path.rs) with the product ACP workspace-file cases and the cross-root grant. The fsModule injection is replaced by the real file system; Windows identity falls back to size and mtime as in the product.

groups.name: Runtime executable discovery
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 with the platform half (login-shell environment, bounded probes, discovery I/O budget, installation definitions, candidate identity and the executable resolver) on the real file system; the product's fsModule/spawn fakes are replaced by temporary executables and an injectable probe runner. Verified live against the installed Codex (login shell, version probe, app-server inspection). Native process ownership reporting for probes is pending.

groups.name: Cursor runtime
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 with the product Cursor adapter and discovery tests on a scripted ACP connection. Live wiring follows the runtime switch.

groups.name: Local Agent probes
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1; codex-local-probe and the local inventory tools are ported with the local-agent inventory.

groups.name: Hermes runtime
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the shared ACP adapter with the product adapter and discovery tests (scripted ACP connection, injected discover/probe). Live wiring follows the runtime switch.

groups.name: OpenCode protocol profile
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the shared ACP adapter with the product adapter and discovery tests (scripted ACP connection, injected discover/probe). Live wiring follows the runtime switch.

groups.name: OpenCode native runtime
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the shared ACP adapter with the product adapter and discovery tests (scripted ACP connection, injected discover/probe). Live wiring follows the runtime switch.

groups.name: WorkBuddy runtime
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 onto the shared ACP adapter with the product adapter and discovery tests (scripted ACP connection, injected discover/probe). Live wiring follows the runtime switch.

groups.name: Pi runtime
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 (the re-export modules map to protocols/pi_rpc) with the product Pi adapter and discovery tests on a scripted client and real temporary executables. Live wiring follows the runtime switch.

groups.name: Process-local cache and quit coordination
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 with the product persistence and shutdown tests: bounded, redacted, process-local recovery events (the legacy durable journal is removed once and never recreated), and quit held until Agent sessions and runtime resources drain. agent-persistence.mjs is a deprecated re-export of the cache. Wiring follows the host switch to AgentService.

groups.name: Production runtime composition
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 with the product production-composition test: the nine runtime definitions (Built-in Agent, Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Cursor, Hermes, Pi and both WorkBuddy channels) in one registry with Codex as the default and per-runtime discovery isolation. The app still composes sessions through legacy_create_agent_runtime_host.rs until the host switches to AgentService.

groups.name: Agent IPC bridge
groups.remaining: Ported 1:1 with the product IPC-authorization and reference-IPC tests: every agent:* channel is parsed against the shared contract, its root authorized before the service runs, turn references authorized and staged snapshots leased per turn (released when the dispatch fails), and failures returned as the operation-failure envelope. Project-session fences are not wired (no project-session service yet); the production composition of electron/main.mjs runs on a dedicated Agent host thread (src/agent/host) that windows reach through AgentHostHandle (invoke, per-window frame sinks, open-project root authorization, close and drain); the GPUI client still talks to the legacy runtimes until the Renderer controllers move onto that handle.
